---
title: "Releases"
description: "What changed in OPDI release v2.0.0 compared with release v0.0.2, and how to move code from the old files and names to the new ones."
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("../../R/portal_config.R")
cfg <- portal_cfg
rel <- portal_release
v2_current <- rel$is_current(cfg)
```

This page compares the two releases of OPDI data: release
`r cfg$release` and the earlier release, `r cfg$previous_release`. It says
what is new for a user of the data, and it gives a table to move code written
for the old files to the new ones.

```{r status}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
if (v2_current) {
  cat("Release ", cfg$release, " is the current release. It covers the days ",
      rel$coverage_text(cfg), ". Release ", cfg$previous_release,
      " stays available but is no longer extended.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("Release ", cfg$release, " is the upcoming release; its files are being produced. ",
      "Until they are available, release ", cfg$current_release, " is the one to use. ",
      "It covers ", portal_labels$month_range(cfg$coverage$start, cfg$coverage$end),
      " and will not be extended.\n", sep = "")
}
```

A **release** is a set of files produced by one version of the OPDI software,
with one set of names and meanings. Every row of release `r cfg$release` says
which release it belongs to, in its column `release`. Older releases are
listed on the [Roadmap](../roadmap.qmd#past-releases).

## What is new in release v2.0.0

### One file per day, and events with their measurements

Release v0.0.2 had three kinds of files: a flight list per month, and flight
events and measurements in separate files of ten days each. Release v2.0.0
has two files per day:

- the **flight list**, one row per flight, and
- the **flight events**, one row per event. Each row carries the event's
  measurements as columns, and the columns of its flight.

A measurement no longer needs a join to its event, and an event no longer
needs a join to its flight. The separate measurements files are no longer
produced. A day's files hold the flights first seen that day, with all their
events, also those after midnight (see [Data](index.qmd#which-day-a-flight-belongs-to)).

### Worldwide coverage

Release v0.0.2 covered a box around Europe. Release v2.0.0 covers every
flight that the OpenSky Network received, anywhere in the world.

### More event types

Release v2.0.0 adds these event families (all listed on the
[Data dictionary](dictionary.qmd#event-types)):

- **Runway milestones**: the start of the take-off roll, the take-off time
  (`ATOT`), the passage over the runway threshold (`landing`), the touchdown
  (`ALDT`), the line-up, the runway vacated, runway crossings and go-arounds.
- **Block times**: off-block (`AOBT`) and in-block (`AIBT`), when the aircraft
  leaves and reaches its parking position.
- **Distance rings**: crossings of circles of 40 to 120 NM around the
  departure and destination airports.
- **Level-offs**: periods of level flight during the climb and the descent.
- **Holding**: the start and end of each holding pattern, with its duration,
  distance and number of loops.
- **Point merge**: the legs of point merge arrival procedures, with their time
  and distance.
- **FIR crossings**: each passage from one flight information region to the
  next.

### A richer flight list

The flight list now holds the main times of each flight, copied from its
events: take-off and landing times, off-block and in-block times, the runways
and stands used, and the times of crossing the distance rings. It also says
how each airport was decided (`adep_source`, `ades_source`) and whether a row
counts as a departure or an arrival (`movement_dep`, `movement_arr`). Column
names are now in lower case.

### One flight across a reception gap

When an aircraft is out of range of every receiver for more than 30 minutes,
for example over an ocean, release v0.0.2 started a new flight after the gap.
Release v2.0.0 keeps one flight when the data on both sides of the gap fit one
continuous flight (see [Track identity](../methods/track-identity.qmd)). Long
flights are therefore more often one row, with both airports.

### Cleaner positions

Repeated, impossible and isolated values in the position reports are removed
before any event is detected (see
[Trajectory cleaning](../methods/trajectory-cleaning.qmd)).

### Documented and checked methods

Each method has a page in [Methods](../methods/index.qmd) that explains how it
works, what it was compared with, how accurate it is and where it fails. The
[Validation summary](../methods/validation-summary.qmd) gives the accuracy of
every item on one page.

### Access through Trino

The files can be queried with SQL on the OpenSky Network's Trino instance,
without downloading them (see [Access](access.qmd)).

## Changes in meaning

Some names stay the same but their meaning or method changed. Code that used
them needs a check.

| Name | In release v0.0.2 | In release v2.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `landing` | The first position on the ground after the descent. | The passage over the runway threshold, a few seconds before touchdown. The touchdown is `ALDT`. |
| `top-of-climb`, `top-of-descent` | The start and end of the cruise, from flight phases. | The method of EUROCONTROL's vertical flight efficiency indicators (see [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd)). |
| `flight_id` (`ID`) | Built from the address, the call sign and the month. | Built from the address and the time of the first position (see [Dictionary](dictionary.qmd#identifiers)). The identifiers of the two releases do not match. |
| `adep`, `ades` | Nearest airport within 30 NM, from positions below 4,000 ft. | A new method that can also leave an airport undecided (see [Departure and destination airports](../methods/airports.qmd)). |

## Moving from v0.0.2 {#moving-from-v0.0.2}

The table lists each file, column or event type of release v0.0.2 and what
replaces it in release v2.0.0.

| Release v0.0.2 | Release v2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `flight_list/flight_list_YYYYMM.parquet`, one file per month | `flight_list/flight_list_YYYYMMDD.parquet`, one file per day |
| `flight_events/flight_events_YYYYMMDD_YYYYMMDD.parquet`, one file per ten days | `flight_events/flight_events_YYYYMMDD.parquet`, one file per day |
| `measurements/measurements_YYYYMMDD_YYYYMMDD.parquet`, one file per ten days | No file. The measurements are columns of the flight events file. |
| Flight list `ID` | `flight_id` |
| Flight list `ICAO24`, `FLT_ID`, `DOF`, `ADEP`, `ADES`, `ADEP_P`, `ADES_P`, `REGISTRATION`, `MODEL`, `TYPECODE`, `ICAO_AIRCRAFT_CLASS`, `ICAO_OPERATOR`, `FIRST_SEEN`, `LAST_SEEN`, `VERSION` | The same names in lower case: `icao24`, `flt_id`, `dof`, and so on |
| Events `id` | `event_id` |
| Events `altitude` (feet) | `altitude_ft` (feet) |
| Events `flight_id`, `type`, `event_time`, `longitude`, `latitude`, `source`, `version`, `info` | The same names |
| Measurements with `type` = `Distance flown (NM)` | Column `distance_flown_nm` |
| Measurements with `type` = `Time Passed (s)` | Column `time_passed_s` |
| Measurements `id`, `event_id`, `value`, `version` | Rebuilt by the `measurements` view: `id` is the `event_id` followed by `_d` (distance) or `_t` (time) |
| Event `take-off` | `ATOT` |
| Event `landing` (first position on the ground) | `ALDT` (touchdown). The name `landing` now means the passage over the threshold. |
| Events `first-xing-fl{level}` and `last-xing-fl{level}` | `xing-fl{level}` for every crossing. The first crossing has `crossing_seq` 1 in `info`; the last has the highest `crossing_seq` of that level on the flight. `direction` in `info` says `up` or `down`. |
| Events `entry-runway` and `exit-runway` | `line-up`, `runway-vacated`, `runway-crossing-entry` and `runway-crossing-vacated`, which say what the aircraft did on the runway |
| Events `entry-taxiway`, `exit-taxiway`, `entry-parking_position`, `exit-parking_position` | The same names |
| Area covered: a box around Europe | The whole world. To keep the old area, filter on the airports or on the event positions. |

### Getting the old shapes

Ready-made views give the data the shape of release v0.0.2, for code written
for that release:

The views have the same names in Trino and in DuckDB.

| Old shape | Trino and DuckDB view | Python reader |
|---|---|---|
| Flight list (lower-case names and order of v0.0.2, 16 columns) | `flight_list_v0` | `published.as_flight_list_v0(flights)` |
| Flight events (without measurements) | `events` | `published.as_events(events)` |
| Measurements (one row per value) | `measurements` | `published.as_measurements(events)` |

[Access](access.qmd) shows how to use them. The views change the shape, not
the content: the rows follow the methods of release v2.0.0, and the
identifiers are text and do not match the 64-bit integer identifiers of
release v0.0.2, so rows cannot be joined to v0.0.2 files by identifier. The
column `version` holds the version of each method, not "v0.0.2". In the
`measurements` view every event has one row for the distance flown and one for
the time passed, even when the value is empty, as in release v0.0.2; the other
measurement types have a row only when they have a value. The old flight list
view leaves out the columns that release v0.0.2 did not have.

## Where release v0.0.2 is

Its files stay available for download on
[Release v0.0.2](v0.0.2.qmd), which also describes how it was
computed.
